questions.question: Which of the following is justiciable in nature?
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, __**Fundamental Rights**__.

__
 
• There are six Fundamental Rights__ in the Indian Constitution and they are as follows:

 
 
• Right to equality
 
• Right to freedom
 
• Right against exploitation
 
• Right to freedom of religion
 
• Cultural and educational right
 
• Right to constitutional remedies
 
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are justiciable in nature.

**Extra facts:**

 
• Article 21A is added in the Indian Constitution in the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002.

 
• Article 19 to 22 comes under the Right to freedom of the Fundamental Right of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: What is the common characteristic of the elements of the same group in the periodic table?

options.text: Electrons in the outer most shell

questions.solution: Elements of the same group in a periodic table have an identical electronic configuration which means they have same outer shell electronsand these outer electrons are called valence electrons. These valence electrons are used for making chemical bonds with other elements.Elements in the same group in the periodic table have similar chemical properties.

questions.question: With which neighboring country of India, Kaladan multi-model transport project has been undertaken?
questions.solution: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project has been undertaken with the neighboring country Myanmar. According to the project, it will connect the eastern Indian seaport of Kolkata with Sittwe seaport in Rakhine State, Myanmar. In Myanmar, it will then link Sittwe seaport to Paletwa, Chin State via the Kaladan river boat route, and then from Paletwa by road to Mizoram state in Northeast India.

questions.question: Which among the following determines the pitch of a sound?
questions.solution: The pitch of a sound depends on the frequency of the source of the sound. Frequency is measured in Hertz (Hz), with one vibration per second being equal to one hertz (1 Hz). A high frequency generally produces a high pitched note and a low frequency similarly produces a low pitched note.

questions.question: Which among the following is also called as 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.solution:
• ‘Mitochondria’ is known as the powerhouse of the cell.
 
• It is found in the cells of both plant and animals.
 
• There are many enzymes and coenzymes which are responsible for energy metabolism.
 
• Mitochondria are the major sites of aerobic respiration within cells since they produce 95 per cent of the ATP molecules in animal cells.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments is also known as the 'Mini Constitution' of India?
questions.solution:
The Forty-second Amendment of India, officially known as The Constitution Act, 1976, was enacted during the Emergency by the Indian National Congress. This amendment brought some of the most important changes to the Constitution in its history. Hence it is sometimes called as “mini-Constitution” of India. Some of the changes that it brought are:

 
• Added Fundamental Duties by the citizens
 
• Made the president bound by the advice of the cabinet.
 
• Provided for administrative tribunals and tribunals for other matters
 
• Froze the seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies on the basis of 1971 census till 2001.
 
• Made the constitutional amendments beyond judicial scrutiny

questions.question: What is the role of Pneumatophores?
questions.solution: Pneumatophores, also called air root are mainly specialized root that grows upwards out of the water or mud to reach the air and from there it obtains oxygen for the root systems of trees that live in swampy or tidal habitats. Ex-The"knees" of mangroves and the bald cypress are examples of pneumatophores.

questions.question: Which among the following is not a direct tax?
questions.solution: A direct tax is paid directly by an individual or organization to the imposing entity. For example, a taxpayer pays direct taxes to the government for various reasons and it includes real property tax, corporate tax, income tax or taxes on assets. All these taxes are paid directly to the government. If a person makes 100,000 in a year and owes 40,000 in taxes, the 40,000 would be a direct tax.

questions.question: Who is called as 'Father of Modern Computer'?
questions.solution: Charles Babbage is known as the 'Father of Modern Computer'after he invented the Analytical Engine in 1837. The Analytical Engine contained an Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), basic flow control, and integrated memory; hailed as the first general-purpose computer concept.

questions.solution: 'Pregnancy Aid Scheme' scheme was launched by P. M. questions.question: Who pioneered diagnostic ultrasound?
questions.solution: Ian Donald, a Scottish physician pioneered the use of diagnostic ultrasound.Medical ultrasound is a diagnostic imaging technique based on the application of ultrasound. It is generally used to see the internal structures such as tendons, muscles, joints, blood vessels, and internal organs of the human body.

questions.question: Courier service comes under which sector?
questions.solution: Courier service comes under the tertiary sector or service sector that is the third of the three economic sectors of the three-sector theory. The others are the secondary sector (the same as manufacturing), and the primary sector (raw materials).

questions.question: What is the full form of ITCZ?
questions.solution:
The full form of **ITCZ **is The **Intertropical Convergence Zone**.

 
• It is the area encircling Earth near the Equator, where there is a convergence of the northeast and southeast trade winds takes place.
 
• The ITCZ was originally identified from the 1920s to the 1940s as the "Intertropical Front" but after the recognition in the 1940s and 1950s of the significance of wind field convergence in tropical weather production.

questions.question: Alps mountain range is located in which continent?
questions.solution: The Alps are the highest and most extensive mountain range system that are located in Europe. The mountain stretches approximately 1,200 kilometers across eight Alpine countries, namely: France, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, and Slovenia.
